questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: The tourists visited ___ church in the village.
questions.explanation: The is used because they visited as sightseers, not for worship.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: The patient is in ___ hospital.
questions.explanation: No article is used before hospital for the purpose of treatment.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: The doctor is at ___ hospital now.
questions.explanation: The is used because the doctor works there and it is a specific place for him.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He was sent to ___ school at six.
questions.explanation: No article is used before school for the purpose of studying.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: The parents went to ___ school to meet the teacher.
questions.explanation: The is used because they went for a different purpose, not to study.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: They are at ___ sea now.
questions.explanation: No article is used in the fixed phrase at sea meaning sailing.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: The children are playing at ___ sea beach.
questions.explanation: The is used before sea beach as a specific place.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He is ___ university professor.
questions.explanation: University begins with the consonant sound yu, so use a.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ professor entered the class.
questions.explanation: The is used because the professor is known to the speaker.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences uses articles correctly? [cow colours]
questions.option_a: A black and a white cow was grazing.
questions.option_b: The black and white cow were grazing.
questions.option_c: Black and white cow was grazing.
questions.option_d: A black and white cow was grazing.
questions.explanation: One article before two adjectives means one cow of two colours.

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence in which the articles are used correctly. [two cows]
questions.option_a: The black and the white cow was grazing.
questions.option_b: A black and a white cow were grazing.
questions.option_c: A black and white cow were grazing.
questions.option_d: Black and white cows was grazing.
questions.explanation: Two articles mean two different cows, so the verb is plural.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence with the correct use of articles. [two officers]
questions.option_a: The chairman and the secretary have resigned.
questions.option_c: The chairman and secretary have resigned.
questions.option_d: The chairman and the secretary has resigned.
questions.explanation: Two articles mean two different persons, so the verb is plural.

questions.question_text: Which sentence is correct with respect to the use of articles? [one officer]
questions.option_a: The chairman and the secretary has resigned.
questions.option_b: The chairman and secretary has resigned.
questions.option_c: The chairman and secretary have resigned.
questions.option_d: The chairman and a secretary has resigned.
questions.explanation: One article means one person holding both posts, so the verb is singular.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ water of this pond is dirty.
questions.explanation: The is used because the water is made specific by the phrase.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ wisdom of Solomon was famous.
questions.explanation: The is used because the wisdom is made specific.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ wisdom is better than wealth.
questions.explanation: No article is used before an abstract noun in a general sense.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ gold of this ring is pure.
questions.explanation: The is used because the gold is made specific.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He has ___ good knowledge of English.
questions.explanation: The phrase is a good knowledge of.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ knowledge he gained was useful.
questions.explanation: The is used because the knowledge is made specific by the clause.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: She plays ___ violin in the orchestra.
questions.explanation: The is used before the names of musical instruments.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He bought ___ violin yesterday.
questions.explanation: A is used for one unspecific violin.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ English language is rich in vocabulary.
questions.explanation: The is used before a language name followed by the word language.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ English spoken here is easy.
questions.explanation: The is used before a language made specific by a phrase.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ French they speak in Canada is different.
questions.explanation: The is used before a language made specific by a clause.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ history of Islam is glorious.
questions.explanation: The is used because the history is made specific.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He is studying ___ history.
questions.explanation: No article is used before history in a general sense.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ nature of his illness is unknown.
questions.explanation: The is used in the phrase the nature of.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: We should protect ___ nature.
questions.explanation: No article is used before nature in a general sense.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences uses articles correctly? [both the boys]
questions.option_a: The both of boys were absent.
questions.explanation: Both comes before the, never after it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of articles? [the both players]
questions.explanation: Both comes before the, never after it.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: I like ___ music of Tagore.
questions.explanation: The is used because the music is made specific.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: She is fond of ___ music.
questions.explanation: No article is used before music in a general sense.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ rice of Dinajpur is famous.
questions.explanation: The is used because the rice is made specific.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ rice is the staple food here.
questions.explanation: No article is used before rice in a general sense.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He had ___ dinner with us.
questions.explanation: No article is used before the names of meals.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ dinner we had was delicious.
questions.explanation: The is used because the dinner is made specific by the clause.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: We take ___ breakfast early.
questions.explanation: No article is used before the names of meals.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ breakfast was served at seven.
questions.explanation: The is used because it refers to a specific breakfast.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence in which the article is used incorrectly. [honourable person]
questions.explanation: An is used before honourable because the h is silent.

questions.question_text: Which sentence has a mistake in the use of articles? [heiress]
questions.option_c: She is an heiress to the estate.
questions.option_d: She is a heiress to the estate.
questions.explanation: An is used before heiress because the h is silent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of articles? [SOS call]
questions.explanation: An is used before SOS because S is pronounced es.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ elephant is a large animal.
questions.explanation: An elephant represents the whole class in a general statement.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ tiger is a fierce animal.
questions.explanation: A tiger represents the whole class in a general statement.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ ant is an industrious insect.
questions.explanation: An ant represents the whole class in a general statement.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: Man is ___ social animal.
questions.explanation: A is used before a singular countable noun in a general statement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences uses articles correctly? [unemployed]
questions.explanation: The is used before an adjective to mean the whole class.

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence in which the articles are used correctly. [deaf]
questions.explanation: The is used before an adjective to mean the whole class.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ dead were buried with honour.
questions.explanation: The is used before an adjective to mean the whole class.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ sick need proper care.
questions.explanation: The is used before an adjective to mean the whole class.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He is ___ one-man army.
questions.explanation: One begins with the consonant sound w, so use a.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: She is ___ once-famous singer.
questions.explanation: Once begins with the consonant sound w, so use a.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: It was ___ one-in-a-million chance.
questions.explanation: One begins with the consonant sound w, so use a.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He gave ___ one-word reply.
questions.explanation: One begins with the consonant sound w, so use a.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ one thing I know is honesty.
questions.explanation: The is used in the phrase the one thing.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ only child of his parents, he was spoilt.
questions.explanation: The is used before only child.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: He is ___ only son of his father.
questions.explanation: The is used before only son.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: ___ first and the last chapters are easy.
questions.explanation: The is used before first and last for specific chapters.

questions.question_text: My birthday is ___ May.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with months.

questions.question_text: The baby sleeps ___ night.
questions.explanation: 'At night' is a fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: Our classes start ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with days of the week.

questions.question_text: She was born ___ 2010.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with years.

questions.question_text: The bus arrives ___ 7 o'clock.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' with clock times.

questions.question_text: I play football ___ the afternoon.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with parts of the day.

questions.question_text: We visit our grandparents ___ Christmas Day.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with specific days and dates.

questions.question_text: Many people rest ___ the weekend.
questions.explanation: 'At the weekend' is the standard British English form.

questions.question_text: Birds fly to warm countries ___ winter.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with seasons.

questions.question_text: He lives ___ Dhaka.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with cities.

questions.question_text: She is waiting ___ the station.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for points such as stations and stops.

questions.question_text: There are many passengers ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with public transport.

questions.question_text: My bag is ___ the car.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with cars, which are enclosed vehicles.

questions.question_text: Dad is ___ home today.
questions.explanation: 'At home' is a fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: Put the book ___ the table.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for surfaces.

questions.question_text: The toys are ___ the box.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' for enclosed spaces.

questions.question_text: The cat is sleeping ___ the bed.
questions.explanation: 'Under' means below something.

questions.question_text: The shop is ___ the school.
questions.explanation: 'Next to' means beside.

questions.question_text: There is a small garden ___ the house.
questions.explanation: 'Behind' means at the back of.

questions.question_text: The bench stands ___ two trees.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used with two things.

questions.question_text: The teacher stood ___ the class.
questions.explanation: 'In front of' means facing or ahead of.

questions.question_text: A picture hangs ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for things attached to a surface.

questions.question_text: They are sitting ___ the room.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' for inside a room.

questions.question_text: He knocked ___ the door.
questions.explanation: 'Knock at the door' is the fixed collocation.

questions.question_text: The exam is ___ Friday.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with days.

questions.question_text: We have lunch ___ noon.
questions.explanation: 'At noon' is a fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: She reads a story ___ the evening.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with parts of the day.

questions.question_text: The train left ___ midnight.
questions.explanation: 'At midnight' is a fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: Bangladesh became independent ___ 1971.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with years.

questions.question_text: We met him ___ the airport.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for points like airports.

questions.question_text: You must finish the work ___ Friday.
questions.explanation: 'By' means not later than — it marks a deadline.

questions.question_text: He will stay in Dhaka ___ next week.
questions.explanation: 'Until' means continuing up to a point in time.

questions.question_text: The lights went out ___ the storm.
questions.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun and means 'in the course of'.

questions.question_text: He has lived here ___ 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with the starting point of an action continuing to now.

questions.question_text: I will be ready ___ an hour.
questions.explanation: 'In' with a future period means after that time has passed.

questions.question_text: She arrived ___ time and caught the train.
questions.explanation: 'In time' means not too late for something.

questions.question_text: The meeting started ___ time, at 10 sharp.
questions.explanation: 'On time' means punctual, at the planned moment.

questions.question_text: ___ the end, we all agreed.
questions.explanation: 'In the end' means 'finally'.

questions.question_text: ___ the end of the movie, the hero died.
questions.explanation: 'At the end of' points to the final part of something.

questions.question_text: Turn left ___ the corner of the street.
questions.explanation: 'At the corner' marks the turning point.

questions.question_text: The child sat ___ the corner of the room.
questions.explanation: 'In the corner' means inside the angle of a room.

questions.question_text: The bank is ___ the corner of the main street.
questions.explanation: A building at a street junction is 'on the corner'.

questions.question_text: He is ___ university now, studying law.
questions.explanation: 'At university' means enrolled as a student.

questions.question_text: The prisoner has been ___ jail for three years.
questions.explanation: 'In jail' means confined as a prisoner.

questions.question_text: We went ___ holiday last summer.
questions.explanation: 'On holiday' is a fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: She learned swimming ___ the age of five.
questions.explanation: 'At the age of' is the fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: She climbed ___ the roof to fix the antenna.
questions.explanation: 'Onto' shows movement to the top of a surface.

questions.question_text: She poured the milk ___ the glass.
questions.explanation: 'Into' shows movement to the inside.

questions.question_text: The dog swam ___ the river to the other bank.
questions.explanation: 'Across' means from one side to the other.

questions.question_text: He walked ___ the tunnel to reach the village.
questions.explanation: 'Through' means inside something, entering one end and leaving the other.

questions.question_text: The river flows ___ the city.
questions.explanation: 'Through' is used for movement within, from end to end.

questions.question_text: They hiked ___ the mountain path all day.
questions.explanation: 'Along' means following the line of something.

questions.question_text: Temperatures stayed ___ zero all week.
questions.explanation: 'Above zero' is the standard phrase for temperature.

questions.question_text: He jumped ___ the fence and ran away.
questions.explanation: 'Over' means above and across to the other side.

questions.question_text: She placed the keys ___ the drawer.
questions.explanation: Keys go inside a drawer, so 'in' is correct.

questions.question_text: The town lies ___ the river and the hills.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used when two landmarks are named.

questions.question_text: The prize was shared ___ the four winners.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used with more than two people.

questions.question_text: She sat ___ me and my brother.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used with two named people.

questions.question_text: The train stopped ___ every small station.
questions.explanation: Stations are points, so we use 'at'.

questions.question_text: He has been ill ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a day as the starting point.

questions.question_text: The goods must reach us ___ the end of this week.
questions.explanation: 'By the end of' sets a deadline — not later than that time.

questions.question_text: The contract is valid ___ three years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time.

questions.question_text: He worked ___ the night to finish the report.
questions.explanation: 'Through the night' means continuing from evening to morning.

questions.question_text: ___ the time we arrived, the show had ended.
questions.explanation: 'By the time' introduces a clause and means 'not later than the moment when'.

questions.question_text: She has been waiting ___ morning.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks when the waiting started.

questions.question_text: The sun rises ___ dawn every day.
questions.explanation: Fixed points like dawn, dusk, noon and midnight take 'at'.

questions.question_text: She waited ___ the top of the stairs.
questions.explanation: 'At the top of' marks the highest point.

questions.question_text: He threw the ball ___ the wall into the garden.
questions.explanation: 'Over' means above and across to the other side.

questions.question_text: The tunnel goes ___ the mountain.
questions.explanation: A tunnel passes inside the mountain, so 'through' is correct.

questions.question_text: He is ___ the committee for cultural affairs.
questions.explanation: Membership of a committee takes 'on'.

questions.question_text: The festival is celebrated ___ the country.
questions.explanation: 'Throughout' means in every part of.

questions.question_text: He sat ___ the shade of the mango tree.
questions.explanation: 'In the shade' is the fixed phrase.

questions.question_text: He stared ___ the window for hours.
questions.explanation: Looking from one side to the other takes 'through'.

questions.question_text: The thief ran ___ the alley and disappeared.
questions.explanation: 'Down the alley' means along its length.

questions.question_text: They sailed ___ the coast for three days.
questions.explanation: 'Along the coast' means following the line of the shore.
We say 'afraid of' before a person, animal, or thing that causes fear.
questions.question_text: She is afraid ___ dogs.

questions.explanation: 'Good at' is the fixed expression for skill in a subject or activity.
questions.question_text: He is good ___ mathematics.

questions.explanation: 'Proud of' is the fixed expression; 'proud at/for/to' are not used.
questions.question_text: I am proud ___ my country.

questions.explanation: 'Interested in' is the fixed expression for showing interest.
questions.question_text: She is interested ___ history.

questions.explanation: 'Depend on' is the fixed expression meaning to rely on someone.
questions.question_text: He depends ___ his parents for money.

questions.explanation: 'Full of' describes a container filled with something.
questions.question_text: The room was full ___ smoke.

questions.explanation: 'Married to' is the fixed expression; 'married with' is wrong in standard English.
questions.question_text: He is married ___ a doctor.

questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to' when comparing two things, not 'than'.
questions.question_text: I prefer tea ___ coffee.

questions.explanation: 'Tired of' is the fixed expression for being bored or exhausted by something.
questions.question_text: He is tired ___ the long journey.

questions.explanation: 'Senior to', 'junior to', 'superior to', 'inferior to' always take 'to', never 'than'.
questions.question_text: She is senior ___ me in the office.

questions.explanation: 'Fond of' is the fixed expression for liking something.
questions.question_text: They are fond ___ classical music.

questions.explanation: 'Guilty of' is the fixed legal expression for a crime.
questions.question_text: He was found guilty ___ theft.

questions.explanation: 'Innocent of' is the fixed expression opposite to 'guilty of'.
questions.question_text: She is innocent ___ the crime.

questions.explanation: 'Responsible for' is the fixed expression for being answerable.
questions.question_text: She is responsible ___ the loss.

questions.explanation: 'Capable of' is the fixed expression for having ability.
questions.question_text: He is capable ___ hard work.

questions.explanation: 'Aware of' is the fixed expression for knowing about something.
questions.question_text: She is aware ___ the danger.

questions.explanation: 'Consist of' is the fixed expression for being made up of parts.
questions.question_text: The book consists ___ ten chapters.

questions.explanation: 'Deal in' means to trade in goods; 'deal with' means to handle a person or problem.
questions.question_text: He deals ___ rice in the local market.

questions.explanation: 'Deal with' means to handle or manage a person, problem, or situation.
questions.question_text: She deals ___ customers politely every day.

questions.explanation: 'Jealous of' is the fixed expression for envy toward someone's advantage.
questions.question_text: I am jealous ___ his success.

questions.explanation: 'Faithful to' is the fixed expression for loyalty.
questions.question_text: The dog is faithful ___ its master.

questions.explanation: 'Kind to' is the fixed expression for gentle behavior toward someone.
questions.question_text: He is kind ___ animals.

questions.explanation: 'Angry with' is used before a person; 'angry at' is used before a thing.
questions.question_text: She is angry ___ me for no reason.

questions.explanation: 'Angry at' is used before a thing or situation, not 'angry with'.
questions.question_text: He became angry ___ the bad news.

questions.explanation: 'Grateful to' is used before a person; 'grateful for' is used before a thing.
questions.question_text: I am grateful ___ him for his help.

questions.explanation: 'Blind to' is the fixed expression for failing to notice faults.
questions.question_text: She is blind ___ her own faults.

questions.explanation: 'Weak in' is the fixed expression for poor performance in a subject.
questions.question_text: He is weak ___ English.

questions.explanation: 'Hopeful of' is the fixed expression for expecting a good result.
questions.question_text: She is hopeful ___ success in the exam.

questions.explanation: We use 'in' for towns, cities, countries, and villages.
questions.question_text: They live ___ a small village.

questions.explanation: We say 'sit on a chair' but 'sit in an armchair'.
questions.question_text: He sat ___ the wooden chair.

questions.explanation: 'Object to' is the fixed expression for raising an objection against something.
questions.question_text: He objected ___ the new proposal.

questions.explanation: 'Insist on' is the fixed expression; 'insist to' is incorrect.
questions.question_text: She insisted ___ going alone.

questions.explanation: 'Persist in' means to continue firmly with an effort or belief.
questions.question_text: He persisted ___ his studies despite failure.

questions.explanation: 'Abstain from' is the fixed expression meaning to keep away from.
questions.question_text: You must abstain ___ smoking.

questions.explanation: 'Accede to' means to agree to a request or demand.
questions.question_text: The manager acceded ___ my request.

questions.explanation: 'Boast of' is the fixed expression for proud talk about one's own things.
questions.question_text: She boasts ___ her wealth.

questions.explanation: 'Avail oneself of' means to make use of an opportunity.
questions.question_text: He availed himself ___ the golden opportunity.

questions.explanation: 'Confide in' means to trust someone with a secret.
questions.question_text: He confided his worries ___ his best friend.

questions.explanation: 'Prevail over' means to defeat or win against enemies.
questions.question_text: They finally prevailed ___ their enemies.

questions.explanation: 'Prevail upon' means to persuade someone to do something.
questions.question_text: I shall prevail ___ him to join our team.

questions.explanation: 'Accustomed to' is the fixed expression for being used to something.
questions.question_text: She is accustomed ___ hard work.

questions.explanation: 'Addicted to' is the fixed expression for a harmful habit.
questions.question_text: He is addicted ___ gambling.

questions.explanation: 'Injurious to' is the fixed expression for something harmful.
questions.question_text: Smoking is injurious ___ health.

questions.explanation: 'Accused of' is the fixed legal expression for charging someone with a crime.
questions.question_text: He was accused ___ theft by the police.

questions.explanation: 'Congratulate on' is the fixed expression for praising someone's success.
questions.question_text: She congratulated me ___ my success.

questions.explanation: 'Die of' is used for a disease or illness.
questions.question_text: The old man died ___ cholera.

questions.explanation: 'Die from' is used for a wound, injury, or overwork.
questions.question_text: The soldier died ___ his wounds.

questions.explanation: 'With' is the correct preposition for the instrument used to cut.
questions.question_text: He cut his finger ___ a sharp knife.

questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' is the fixed expression, and 'to' is followed by a noun or gerund.
questions.question_text: She looks forward ___ the holidays.

questions.explanation: 'Attend on' means to visit and care for a sick person, used by doctors and nurses.
questions.question_text: The nurse attended ___ the patient all night.

questions.explanation: 'Attend to' means to give careful attention to duties or lessons.
questions.question_text: You should attend ___ your lessons carefully.

questions.explanation: 'Attribute to' is the fixed expression for assigning a cause.
questions.question_text: The success was attributed ___ hard work.

questions.explanation: Like 'senior' and 'superior', 'inferior to' always takes 'to', never 'than'.
questions.question_text: This cloth is inferior ___ that one in quality.

questions.explanation: 'Superior to' always takes 'to'; 'superior than' is a common error.
questions.question_text: His conduct is superior ___ hers in every way.

questions.explanation: 'Born of' is used for parentage; 'born in' is used for a place.
questions.question_text: She was born ___ rich parents.

questions.explanation: 'Charged with' is the fixed legal expression for accusing someone of a crime.
questions.question_text: He was charged ___ murder by the court.

questions.explanation: 'Dispense with' means to do without something no longer needed.
questions.question_text: She dispensed ___ the maid's services.

questions.explanation: 'Sympathize with' is the fixed expression for sharing someone's sorrow.
questions.question_text: He sympathized ___ me in my grief.

questions.explanation: 'Interfere in' is used for meddling in affairs or disputes.
questions.question_text: The teacher interfered ___ the quarrel to stop it.

questions.explanation: 'Apologize to' is used before a person; 'apologize for' is used before the fault.
questions.question_text: He apologized ___ me for his rudeness.

questions.explanation: 'Agree to' is used before a proposal or offer; 'agree with' is used before a person.
questions.question_text: He agreed ___ my proposal at once.

questions.explanation: 'Agree with' is used before a person or opinion, not before a proposal.
questions.question_text: I agree ___ you on this point.

questions.explanation: 'Agree on' is used before a matter or plan that both sides accept.
questions.question_text: They finally agreed ___ a date for the meeting.

questions.explanation: 'Compare with' is used when noting similarities or differences between similar things.
questions.question_text: She compares her dress ___ mine.

questions.explanation: 'Compare to' is used when likening one thing to another of a different kind.
questions.question_text: The poet compared life ___ a dream.

questions.explanation: 'Correspond with' is used for exchanging letters with a person.
questions.question_text: He corresponds ___ his brother regularly.

questions.explanation: 'Correspond to' means to match or be equivalent to something.
questions.question_text: His actions correspond ___ his words.

questions.explanation: 'Part from' is used for leaving people; 'part with' is used for giving up things.
questions.question_text: She parted ___ her friends in tears.

questions.explanation: 'Part with' is used for giving up a possession, often reluctantly.
questions.question_text: He parted ___ his old watch reluctantly.

questions.explanation: 'Inquire into' means to investigate or examine a matter formally.
questions.question_text: The committee will inquire ___ the matter.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'Was the thief caught?'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'Is the work done?'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The door was not opened.'

questions.option_c: He does not send the letter yet.
questions.option_d: He did not send the letter yet.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'By whom was the letter written?'
questions.explanation: 'By whom' in a past passive question becomes 'Who' with a past active verb: 'Who wrote the letter?'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'What was done by you?'
questions.explanation: Past passive question 'What was done' becomes past active 'What did you do?'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The work should have been done.'

questions.option_c: You should be doing the work.
questions.option_d: You should have been doing the work.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive 'should have been done' becomes modal perfect active 'should have done'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The thief could have been caught.'
questions.option_a: They could have caught the thief.
questions.option_b: They could be catching the thief.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive 'could have been caught' becomes 'could have caught'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The bill must have been paid.'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The letter might have been lost.'

questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive 'might have been lost' becomes 'might have lost'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The work has to be done today.'

questions.option_b: You must do the work today.
questions.option_c: You had to do the work today.
questions.option_d: You have to be doing the work today.
questions.explanation: Semi-modal passive 'has to be done' becomes 'have to do'; the semi-modal is kept, not changed to 'must'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The room is to be cleaned.'

questions.option_c: You ought to finish the work soon.
questions.option_d: You should finish the work soon.
questions.explanation: The modal 'ought to' is kept unchanged: 'ought to be finished' becomes 'ought to finish'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'The gate used to be locked at night.'

questions.option_b: They use to lock the gate at night.
questions.option_c: They used to lock the gate at night.
questions.option_d: They were used to lock the gate at night.
questions.explanation: 'Used to be locked' becomes 'used to lock'; the form 'used to' does not change.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'Let the letter be written by him.'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'Let not the child be beaten.'

questions.question_text: 'The house is to let.' is an example of —

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'She was heard to sing.'

questions.option_b: They saw the thief to run away.
questions.option_c: They see the thief run away.
questions.option_d: They had seen the thief to run away.
questions.explanation: The 'to' of the passive infinitive drops in the active: 'saw the thief run away'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct active voice: 'I was kept waiting for an hour.'

questions.option_b: They have kept me waiting for an hour.
questions.option_c: They had kept me waiting for an hour.
questions.option_d: They keep me waiting for an hour.

questions.option_d: People thought he has left the country.

questions.option_c: He told me that he would see you the next day.
questions.option_d: He said me that he would see me the next day.
questions.explanation: 'said to me' -> 'told me'; 'shall' -> 'would'; 'tomorrow' -> 'the next day'.

questions.question_text: She said, "My father will come here tonight." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that her father will come here tonight.
questions.option_b: She said that her father would come there that night.
questions.option_c: She said that her father would come here that night.
questions.option_d: She told that her father would come there that night.
questions.explanation: 'will' -> 'would'; 'here' -> 'there'; 'tonight' -> 'that night'.

questions.question_text: He said, "We went there last month and enjoyed ourselves." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that they went there last month and enjoyed themselves.
questions.option_b: He said that they had gone there last month and enjoyed themselves.
questions.option_c: He said that they had gone there the previous month and had enjoyed themselves.
questions.option_d: He told that they had gone there the previous month and had enjoyed themselves.
questions.explanation: Both past simple verbs become past perfect; 'last month' -> 'the previous month'.

questions.question_text: He said that he was unwell. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.explanation: Past 'was' reverts to present 'am'; 'he' reverts to 'I'.

questions.question_text: She told me that she would help me. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: She said to me, "I shall help you."
questions.option_b: She said to me, "I will help you."
questions.option_c: She said to me, "She would help me."
questions.option_d: She said to me, "I would help you."
questions.explanation: 'would' reverts to 'shall' with first person; 'me' reverts to 'you'.

questions.question_text: He asked me if I knew him. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: He said to me, "Did you know him?"
questions.option_b: He said to me, "Do you know him?"
questions.option_c: He said to me, "Do I know him?"
questions.option_d: He said to me, "If you know him?"
questions.explanation: 'asked if I knew' reverts to the question 'Do you know him?'.

questions.question_text: She asked me where I lived. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: She said to me, "Where did you live?"
questions.option_b: She said to me, "Where I lived?"
questions.option_c: She said to me, "Where do you live?"
questions.option_d: She said to me, "Where do I live?"
questions.explanation: 'asked where I lived' reverts to 'Where do you live?'.

questions.question_text: He ordered me to leave the room. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: He said to me, "You leave the room."
questions.option_b: He said to me, "To leave the room."
questions.option_c: He said to me, "Leave the room, please."
questions.option_d: He said to me, "Leave the room."
questions.explanation: 'ordered me to leave' reverts to the imperative 'Leave the room.'

questions.question_text: She requested me to help her. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: She said to me, "Please help me."
questions.option_c: She said to me, "To help me."
questions.option_d: She said to me, "You help me."
questions.explanation: 'requested me to help her' reverts to 'Please help me.'

questions.question_text: He wished that I might succeed. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.explanation: 'wished that I might' reverts to the optative 'May you succeed!'.

questions.question_text: She exclaimed with joy that they had won. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.explanation: 'exclaimed with joy that they had won' reverts to 'Hurrah! We have won.'

questions.question_text: He said that the earth is round. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_b: He said, "The earth has been round."
questions.explanation: Universal truths stay in the present tense in both forms.

questions.question_text: They told us that they had seen the match. Choose the correct direct speech.
questions.option_a: They said to us, "We have seen the match."
questions.option_b: They said to us, "We had seen the match."
questions.option_c: They said to us, "They have seen the match."
questions.option_d: They said to us, "We have saw the match."
questions.explanation: 'had seen' reverts to 'have seen'; 'they' reverts to 'we'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correctly reported sentence.
questions.option_a: He said his sister that he was busy.
questions.option_b: He told his sister that he was busy.
questions.option_c: He said to his sister that he is busy.
questions.option_d: He told to his sister that he was busy.
questions.explanation: 'told' needs an object and is followed by 'that'; tense shifts to past.

questions.question_text: Choose the correctly reported question.
questions.option_a: She asked me that where I lived.
questions.option_b: She asked me where did I live.
questions.option_c: She asked me where I lived.
questions.option_d: She asked to me where I lived.
questions.explanation: No 'that' after 'asked'; no inversion in the reported clause.

questions.question_text: Choose the correctly reported command.
questions.option_a: He ordered me that to go.
questions.option_b: He ordered to me to go.
questions.option_c: He ordered that me to go.
questions.explanation: Pattern: 'ordered' + object + to-infinitive, no 'that'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correctly reported exclamation.
questions.option_a: She exclaimed with joy that it was a very beautiful flower.
questions.option_b: She exclaimed with joy that what a beautiful flower it was.
questions.option_c: She said with joy that it was a very beautiful flower.
questions.option_d: She exclaimed with joy that it is a very beautiful flower.
questions.explanation: 'What a ...!' becomes 'a very ...' with past tense.

questions.question_text: He said, "I am going to Dhaka tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he is going to Dhaka tomorrow.
questions.option_b: He said that he was going to Dhaka the next day.
questions.option_c: He said that he was go to Dhaka the next day.
questions.option_d: He told that he was going to Dhaka the next day.
questions.explanation: 'am going to' -> 'was going to'; 'tomorrow' -> 'the next day'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence is in indirect speech?
questions.option_c: She said that she was tired.
questions.option_d: She said me that she was tired.
questions.explanation: Indirect speech has no quotation marks and uses 'that'.

questions.question_text: The boy said to the girl, "I love you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: The boy said to the girl that I love you.
questions.option_b: The boy told the girl that he loved you.
questions.option_c: The boy said the girl that he loved her.
questions.option_d: The boy told the girl that he loved her.
questions.explanation: 'said to the girl' -> 'told the girl'; 'I' -> 'he'; 'you' -> 'her'.

questions.question_text: I said to my friend, "Let us play." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: I proposed to my friend that we should play.
questions.option_b: I said to my friend to play.
questions.option_c: I proposed to my friend that we shall play.
questions.option_d: I told my friend that we should play.
questions.explanation: 'Let us' -> 'proposed ... that we should'.

questions.question_text: She said to me, "May you be happy!" Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said to me that you may be happy.
questions.option_b: She wished that I might be happy.
questions.option_c: She wished that you might be happy.
questions.option_d: She prayed that I may be happy.
questions.explanation: Optative: 'wished that I might'.

questions.question_text: He said, "Good bye, friends!" Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that good bye friends.
questions.option_b: He told his friends that good bye.
questions.option_c: He bade his friends good bye.
questions.option_d: He wished his friends that good bye.
questions.explanation: Parting is reported with 'bade ... good bye'.

questions.question_text: She said, "Sorry for the delay." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that sorry for the delay.
questions.option_b: She told that sorry for the delay.
questions.explanation: An apology is reported with 'apologised for'.

questions.question_text: He said to me, "Beware of pickpockets." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_b: He said to me to beware of pickpockets.
questions.option_c: He warned to me against pickpockets.
questions.option_d: He told me that to beware of pickpockets.
questions.explanation: 'Beware of ...' becomes 'warned me against ...'.

questions.question_text: The judge said, "Let the prisoner be set free." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: The judge said to let the prisoner be set free.
questions.option_b: The judge ordered that the prisoner should be set free.
questions.option_c: The judge ordered to the prisoner to be set free.
questions.option_d: The judge told that the prisoner should be set free.
questions.explanation: An authoritative 'let' command: 'ordered that ... should'.

questions.question_text: He said, "Let me go now." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said to let him go now.
questions.option_b: He ordered to be allowed to go then.
questions.option_c: He requested to be allowed to go then.
questions.option_d: He told to be allowed to go now.
questions.explanation: 'Let me go' -> 'requested to be allowed to go'; 'now' -> 'then'.

questions.question_text: She said to me, "Do you know the answer?" Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She asked me that I knew the answer.
questions.option_b: She asked me do I know the answer.
questions.option_c: She told me if I knew the answer.
questions.option_d: She asked me if I knew the answer.
questions.explanation: Yes/no question: 'asked' + 'if' + assertive clause.

questions.question_text: He said, "I must go now, for it is getting late." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he had to go then, for it was getting late.
questions.option_b: He said that he must go now, for it is getting late.
questions.option_c: He said that he has to go then, for it was getting late.
questions.option_d: He told that he had to go then, for it was getting late.
questions.explanation: 'must' as a present obligation becomes 'had to'; both clauses backshift.

questions.question_text: She said, "You must not enter the room." Reported to me, choose the correct form.
questions.option_a: She told me that I had not to enter the room.
questions.option_b: She told me that I must not enter the room.
questions.option_c: She said to me that you must not enter the room.
questions.option_d: She told to me that I must not enter the room.
questions.explanation: 'must not' expressing prohibition stays 'must not'.

questions.question_text: He said, "I must have left my keys at home." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he had to have left his keys at home.
questions.option_b: He said that he must had left my keys at home.
questions.option_c: He said that he must have left his keys at home.
questions.option_d: He told that he must have left his keys at home.
questions.explanation: 'must have' expressing deduction remains unchanged.

questions.question_text: She said, "If I were rich, I would travel the world." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that if she had been rich, she would have travelled the world.
questions.option_b: She said that if she was rich, she will travel the world.
questions.option_c: She told that if she were rich, she would travel the world.
questions.option_d: She said that if she were rich, she would travel the world.
questions.explanation: Unreal conditionals (type 2) do not change in indirect speech.

questions.question_text: He said, "If you had worked hard, you would have passed." Reported to me, choose the correct form.
questions.option_a: He told me that if I had worked hard, I would have passed.
questions.option_b: He told me that if I worked hard, I would pass.
questions.option_c: He told me that if I have worked hard, I will have passed.
questions.option_d: He said to me that if you had worked hard, you would have passed.
questions.explanation: Type 3 conditionals remain unchanged; only pronouns shift.

questions.question_text: She said, "Had I been there, I would have helped you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that if she had been there, she would help you.
questions.option_b: She said that had she been there, she would have helped me.
questions.option_c: She said that had she been there, she would had helped me.
questions.option_d: She told that had she been there, she would have helped me.
questions.explanation: Inverted conditionals keep their form; pronouns shift.

questions.question_text: He said, "I shall be reading at this time tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he shall be reading at this time tomorrow.
questions.option_b: He said that he would be read at that time the next day.
questions.option_c: He said that he would be reading at that time the next day.
questions.option_d: He told that he would be reading at that time the next day.
questions.explanation: Future continuous 'shall be reading' becomes 'would be reading'.

questions.question_text: She said, "By next June I shall have lived here for five years." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that by next June she shall have lived here for five years.
questions.option_b: She said that by the following June she would had lived there for five years.
questions.option_c: She told that by the following June she would have lived there for five years.
questions.option_d: She said that by the following June she would have lived there for five years.
questions.explanation: Future perfect becomes 'would have lived'; 'next June' -> 'the following June'.

questions.question_text: He said, "I have to attend a meeting today." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he had to attend a meeting that day.
questions.option_b: He said that he has to attend a meeting today.
questions.option_c: He said that he had to attended a meeting that day.
questions.option_d: He told that he had to attend a meeting that day.
questions.explanation: 'have to' becomes 'had to'; 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I have got to finish this now." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she has got to finish this now.
questions.option_b: She said that she had got to finish that then.
questions.option_c: She said that she had got to finished that then.
questions.option_d: She told that she had got to finish that then.
questions.explanation: 'have got to' becomes 'had got to'; 'this' -> 'that'; 'now' -> 'then'.

questions.question_text: He said, "The train leaves at 6 a.m." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that the train left at 6 a.m.
questions.option_b: He said that the train had left at 6 a.m.
questions.option_c: He said that the train leaves at 6 a.m.
questions.option_d: He told that the train leaves at 6 a.m.
questions.explanation: Timetables and scheduled events keep the present tense.

questions.question_text: He said to me, "You had better not waste your time." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He told me that I had better not waste my time.
questions.option_b: He advised to me not to waste my time.
questions.option_c: He said to me not to waste your time.
questions.option_d: He advised me not to waste my time.
questions.explanation: 'You had better not ...' is reported as advice with 'advised ... not to'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I would rather die than beg." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she would rather die than beg.
questions.option_b: She said that she will rather die than beg.
questions.option_c: She said that she would rather died than beg.
questions.option_d: She told that she would rather die than beg.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' does not change.

questions.question_text: He said, "Need I come tomorrow?" Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He asked that he need come tomorrow.
questions.option_b: He asked if he needed to come the next day.
questions.option_c: He asked if he need to come the next day.
questions.option_d: He told if he needed to come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Need I ...?' becomes 'asked if he needed to ...'.

questions.question_text: She said, "You need not come again." Reported to me, choose the correct form.
questions.option_a: She told me that I did not need come again.
questions.option_b: She said to me that you need not come again.
questions.option_c: She told me that I need not come again.
questions.option_d: She told to me that I need not come again.
questions.explanation: 'need not' stays unchanged; 'you' becomes 'I'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I used to smoke, but I have given it up." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she used to smoke, but she has given it up.
questions.option_b: She said that she had used to smoke, but she had given it up.
questions.option_c: She told that she used to smoke, but she had given it up.
questions.option_d: She said that she used to smoke, but she had given it up.
questions.explanation: 'used to' stays; 'have given' becomes 'had given'.

questions.question_text: He said, "I have just received your letter." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he had just received my letter.
questions.option_b: He said that he has just received your letter.
questions.option_c: He said that he had just receive my letter.
questions.option_d: He told that he had just received my letter.
questions.explanation: 'have received' becomes 'had received'; 'your' becomes 'my'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I saw him the day before yesterday." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she saw him the day before yesterday.
questions.option_b: She said that she had seen him two days before.
questions.option_c: She said that she had saw him two days before.
questions.option_d: She told that she had seen him two days before.
questions.explanation: 'the day before yesterday' becomes 'two days before'.

questions.question_text: He said, "I will come here the day after tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he will come here the day after tomorrow.
questions.option_b: He said that he would come here two days after.
questions.option_c: He said that he would come there two days after.
questions.option_d: He told that he would come there two days after.
questions.explanation: 'the day after tomorrow' becomes 'two days after'; 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I bought this book last Monday." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she bought this book last Monday.
questions.option_b: She said that she had bought this book the previous Monday.
questions.option_c: She told that she had bought that book the previous Monday.
questions.option_d: She said that she had bought that book the previous Monday.
questions.explanation: 'bought' -> 'had bought'; 'this' -> 'that'; 'last Monday' -> 'the previous Monday'.

questions.question_text: He said, "We play here every evening." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that they played there every evening.
questions.option_b: He said that they play here every evening.
questions.option_c: He said that they had played there every evening.
questions.option_d: He told that they played there every evening.
questions.explanation: Habitual present simple backshifts to past simple; 'here' -> 'there'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I shall never forget this kindness." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she shall never forget this kindness.
questions.option_b: She said that she would never forget that kindness.
questions.option_c: She said that she would never forgot that kindness.
questions.option_d: She told that she would never forget that kindness.
questions.explanation: 'shall' -> 'would'; 'this' -> 'that'.

questions.question_text: He said, "All that glitters is not gold." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that all that glitters was not gold.
questions.option_b: He said that all that glittered is not gold.
questions.option_c: He said that all that glitters is not gold.
questions.option_d: He told that all that glitters is not gold.
questions.explanation: Proverbs never change tense in indirect speech.

questions.question_text: She said, "I was to leave for London the next day." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she was to leave for London the next day.
questions.option_b: She said that she is to leave for London the next day.
questions.option_c: She told that she had been to leave for London the next day.
questions.option_d: She said that she had been to leave for London the next day.
questions.explanation: 'was to' (past arrangement) becomes 'had been to' when reported later.

questions.question_text: He said, "I am having my lunch now; please come later." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he was having his lunch then and requested me to come later.
questions.option_b: He said that he is having his lunch now and requested me to come later.
questions.option_c: He said that he was having his lunch now and requested me to come later.
questions.option_d: He told that he was having his lunch then and requested me to come later.
questions.explanation: Two clauses: assertive backshifts; the imperative becomes a request.

questions.question_text: He said to me, "Are you coming with us? We are leaving now." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He asked me that I was going with them and said that they were leaving now.
questions.option_b: He asked me if I was going with them and said that they were leaving then.
questions.option_c: He asked me if I am going with us and said that they are leaving then.
questions.option_d: He told me if I was going with them and said that they were leaving then.
questions.explanation: Question -> 'asked if'; statement backshifts; 'us' -> 'them'; 'now' -> 'then'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I am sorry. I broke your pen." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that sorry and she broke your pen.
questions.option_b: She apologised and said that she has broken my pen.
questions.option_c: She apologised and said that she had broken my pen.
questions.option_d: She told and said that she had broken my pen.
questions.explanation: 'I am sorry' -> 'apologised'; 'broke' -> 'had broken'.

questions.question_text: He said to me, "Do not worry. I shall help you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said to me not to worry and said that he shall help you.
questions.option_b: He told me to not worry and said that he would help you.
questions.option_c: He ordered me not to worry and said that he would help me.
questions.option_d: He told me not to worry and said that he would help me.
questions.explanation: Negative imperative -> 'told me not to'; promise backshifts to 'would'.

questions.question_text: She said, "What a pleasant surprise! I did not expect you today." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She exclaimed with joy that it was a very pleasant surprise and said that she had not expected me that day.
questions.option_b: She said that it was a very pleasant surprise and said that she did not expect you today.
questions.option_c: She exclaimed with joy that what a pleasant surprise it was and said that she had not expected me that day.
questions.option_d: She told with joy that it was a very pleasant surprise and said that she had not expected me that day.
questions.explanation: Exclamation -> 'exclaimed with joy'; statement backshifts with 'today' -> 'that day'.

questions.question_text: He said, "Hurrah! I have got the first prize." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he had got the first prize.
questions.option_b: He exclaimed with joy that he had got the first prize.
questions.option_c: He exclaimed with joy that I have got the first prize.
questions.option_d: He told with joy that he had got the first prize.
questions.explanation: 'Hurrah!' -> 'exclaimed with joy'; present perfect -> past perfect.

questions.question_text: The teacher said to the boy, "Why were you absent yesterday? Bring your guardian tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: The teacher asked the boy why was he absent yesterday and ordered him to bring his guardian tomorrow.
questions.option_b: The teacher asked the boy why he was absent the day before and ordered him to bring his guardian the next day.
questions.option_c: The teacher asked the boy why he had been absent the day before and ordered him to bring his guardian the next day.
questions.option_d: The teacher told the boy why he had been absent the day before and ordered him to bring his guardian the next day.
questions.explanation: Question -> 'asked' with backshift; command -> 'ordered ... to'.

questions.question_text: She said to me, "Will you come to my house tomorrow? Mother wants to see you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She asked me that I would go to her house tomorrow and said that her mother wants to see you.
questions.option_b: She asked me if I will come to my house the next day and said that her mother wanted to see me.
questions.option_c: She told me if I would go to her house the next day and said that her mother wanted to see me.
questions.option_d: She asked me if I would go to her house the next day and said that her mother wanted to see me.
questions.explanation: 'come' -> 'go' (perspective shift); both clauses backshift.

questions.question_text: He said, "I do not know the boy who is standing there." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he did not know the boy who was standing there.
questions.option_b: He said that he does not know the boy who is standing there.
questions.option_c: He said that he did not knew the boy who was standing there.
questions.option_d: He told that he did not know the boy who was standing there.
questions.explanation: Main and relative clauses both shift to past tense.

questions.question_text: She said to him, "If you work hard, you will succeed." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She told him that if he works hard, he will succeed.
questions.option_b: She told him that if he worked hard, he would succeed.
questions.option_c: She told him that if you worked hard, you would succeed.
questions.option_d: She said to him that if he worked hard, he would succeed.
questions.explanation: A real (type 1) conditional backshifts like ordinary clauses.

questions.question_text: He said, "I played here when I was a child." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he played here when he was a child.
questions.option_b: He said that he had played there when he had been a child.
questions.option_c: He said that he had played there when he was a child.
questions.option_d: He told that he had played there when he was a child.
questions.explanation: Main clause backshifts; the time clause stays in past simple; 'here' -> 'there'.

questions.question_text: She said, "The man who came here yesterday is my uncle." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that the man who came here yesterday is her uncle.
questions.option_b: She said that the man who had come here the day before was my uncle.
questions.option_c: She told that the man who had come there the day before was her uncle.
questions.option_d: She said that the man who had come there the day before was her uncle.
questions.explanation: Relative clause backshifts; 'here' -> 'there'; 'yesterday' -> 'the day before'.

questions.question_text: He said to me, "You are my best friend, and I shall never forget you." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He told me that I was his best friend and that he would never forget me.
questions.option_b: He said to me that you are my best friend and I shall never forget you.
questions.option_c: He told me that you were his best friend and that he would never forget you.
questions.option_d: He said me that I was his best friend and that he would never forget me.
questions.explanation: Both clauses backshift; 'you' -> 'I'; 'my' -> 'his'.

questions.question_text: She said, "I wish I knew the answer." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: She said that she wishes she knew the answer.
questions.option_b: She said that she wished she knew the answer.
questions.option_c: She said that she wished she had known the answer.
questions.option_d: She told that she wished she knew the answer.
questions.explanation: 'wish' + past subjunctive stays unchanged after backshift of 'wish'.

questions.question_text: He said, "I wish I had met you earlier." Choose the correct indirect speech.
questions.option_a: He said that he wishes he had met you earlier.
